newsitem.title: USA: BADMINTON-TOP MEN SURVIVE AT U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-TOP MEN SURVIVE AT U.S. OPEN.

text.p: The world's top-ranked players in men's singles and men's doubles, all three of them Indonesian, overcame tough Malaysian challenges in Thursday's quarter-finals of the U.S. Open Badminton Championships.
Indonesia's top-seeded pair of Denny Kartono and Antonius survived two tie-breaker sets in an 18-14 16-18 15-2 victory against Malaysia's Lee Wan Wah and Choong Tan Fook, ranked 17th internationally.
Another top-seeded Indonesian, Joko Suprianto, earned a 15-8 3-15 15-12 triumph over 12th-ranked Ong Ewe Hock from Malaysia.

Suprianto, a quarter-finalist at the 1996 Olympics, needed a rally in the third game to win. Ong had a 5-0 lead before Suprianto forced ties of 6-6 and 8-8. The Indonesian then scored the next seven points, including the final five in succession.
"I had to play more offensively," Suprianto said through a translator. "Ong was weak on his left side, so I knew I had to smash to his backhand."

Kantono and Antonius had less difficulty in their decisive third set. The pair scored 10 consecutive points on Antonius's service to take a 13-1 lead. Antonius also scored five of the points off smashes and backhands.

"Most of the time, I used short serves," Antonius said through a translator. "I wanted to make them lift the bird so we could attack them. Their offence was really strong, but sometimes they made easy mistakes."

Among the internationally ranked players advancing to the semifinals was Denmark's Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen, Olympic and All-England champion in men's singles. Hoyer-Larsen is ranked third in the world.
